subsystems.name: Partitioning plant
subsystems.role: separates long-lived actinides from spent fuel so they can be transmuted.

subsystems.name: Transmutation core
subsystems.role: where neutrons convert long-lived isotopes into shorter-lived ones.

subsystems.name: Neutron source
subsystems.role: for accelerator-driven systems, supplies extra neutrons to drive a subcritical core.

subsystems.name: Coolant system
subsystems.role: removes the intense heat from transmutation.

subsystems.name: Fuel fabrication
subsystems.role: makes new targets containing the separated actinides.

subsystems.name: Remote handling and shielding
subsystems.role: protects workers from the extreme radioactivity of the materials.

buildSteps.title: Separate spent fuel
buildSteps.detail: Reprocess used fuel to isolate uranium, plutonium and the minor actinides (americium, curium) that dominate long-term radiotoxicity.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate targets
buildSteps.detail: Mix minor actinides with an inert matrix such as zirconia or a metal alloy, press and sinter them, and seal them in steel cladding.

buildSteps.title: Build the machine
buildSteps.detail: Construct either a fast-neutron reactor or an accelerator-driven system (ADS): a proton accelerator, a spallation target loop, and a subcritical core.

buildSteps.title: Install core and target
buildSteps.detail: Load the actinide-bearing fuel assemblies, connect the coolant loops, and fit the beam window that separates accelerator from target.

buildSteps.title: Start up
buildSteps.detail: Accelerate a proton beam into the target to produce spallation neutrons, or bring the fast reactor critical, and begin transmutation.

buildSteps.title: Operate and cool
buildSteps.detail: Circulate liquid metal or gas to remove heat, monitor how quickly long-lived isotopes are converted, and possibly raise steam.

buildSteps.title: Reprocess and repeat
buildSteps.detail: Recover remaining actinides from the used targets, refabricate them, and run them through the machine again to push conversion further.

buildSteps.title: Dispose of final waste
buildSteps.detail: The remaining waste is far shorter-lived but still needs geological disposal — for a much shorter period than untreated fuel.

prerequisites.why: separating minor actinides from spent fuel has been demonstrated at laboratory and pilot scale but not industrially.
several have operated, but none has been used routinely for waste transmutation at scale.
no industrial ADS exists; MYRRHA in Belgium is a research facility still under construction.
targets have run only at low power; the beam window and liquid-metal loop must survive intense radiation.

prerequisites.tech: Remote handling for highly radioactive materials
prerequisites.why: hot-cell technology is mature from reprocessing and isotope production.
fuel cladding and structural metals degrade quickly under the neutron and proton fluxes involved.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and pilot separation of minor actinides; construction of MYRRHA in Belgium
pathway.unlocks: the chemistry and neutronics needed to design a transmutation system.

pathway.milestone: a demonstration ADS or fast reactor that transmutes minor actinides at significant scale
pathway.unlocks: proof that the process reduces waste radiotoxicity as predicted.

pathway.milestone: an integrated pilot plant combining partitioning, target fabrication and transmutation
pathway.unlocks: reliable operation and cost data for a full-scale facility.

pathway.milestone: commercial transmutation coupled to geological disposal
pathway.unlocks: nuclear waste that stays hazardous for centuries rather than hundreds of millennia.
